subject: Materials Science
title: Carbon Fiber: Light and Mighty
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Carbon Fiber: Light and Mighty.

hook.text: A carbon fiber strand is thinner than a human hair yet five times stronger than steel.

buildup.text: Carbon fiber starts as a polymer precursor — usually PAN — that's heated to 2,000°C in nitrogen.

discovery.text: The heat drives off everything except carbon, which aligns into graphite-like sheets along the fiber.

twist.text: Those aligned carbon bonds give extreme stiffness along the fiber but almost none across it.

climax.text: Formula 1 cars, bicycle frames, and satellite panels all depend on carbon fiber composites.

punchline.text: Burn a polymer away and what's left is the strongest fiber on Earth.

quiz.question: What is carbon fiber made from?
options: A polymer precursor heated until only carbon remains
